title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 23/27 — "Under the Feet of the Martians"
description:
He climbs from the pit onto a rocking mound and finds not ruined Sheen but an alien country remade by red growth. "The fear and empire of man had passed away," he says, feeling the old order leave his body as he turns from the conqueror's throne toward a walled garden and uncertain food.

Hunger drives him down through the crimson stems to brown floodwater spreading over drowned meadows. Thirst wins first; he kneels and drinks the strange current, testing a metallic frond as the red weed that conquered every low field begins to whiten, break, and drift seaward.

He follows ruined lamps uphill to Putney Common, where stripped trees and searched houses offer nothing. Two hungry dogs circle him near scattered bones of cats, a rabbit, and a sheep; he gnaws one remnant and finds the same empty answer as the houses, then digs potatoes after sunset for another hour's strength.

From the brow he looks over black trees, roofless ruins, and sinking red water, asking, "But where are the people?" A dismembered skeleton lies broken on the hilltop, and he understands that almost every life here has already been extinguished — the valley answers only with silence, hunger outliving the people as the red flood keeps moving.

Chapter VI of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "The Work of Fifteen Days", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
